Title: Iranian stuntwomen breaking gender norms with daring feats
Article:
TEHERAN: As evening falls at a Teheran skatepark, a woman calmly steps forward with her body ablaze, performing a daring stunt that challenges convention in front of an impressed Iranian audience.
Behind her, young women practise backward flips into a pit filled with foam, following the instructions of Nasrin Teymouri.
In her thirties, she leads Iran's sole all-female stunt crew, a vital area of filmmaking traditionally controlled by men, but where Iranian women are increasingly establishing themselves.
"Until just a few years ago, men used to dress up as women to perform stunts in place of actresses," said Teymouri with a smile, as she received AFP at a training session for the "Stunt Powerful" team in southern Teheran.
On graffiti-decorated ramps, a young girl wearing roller skates practises a few moves, while a young man gets ready to perform a stunt on his BMX bicycle.
The setting is unusual for this relatively traditional neighbourhood of the Iranian capital.
A huge Islamic republic flag flutters in the distance, while the golden dome of a nearby mosque can be seen from the skatepark.
The site, dedicated to extreme sports and named "Navid Park" after its founder, opened a year ago.
[[nid:1551113]]
"Even prominent directors would bluntly tell us we couldn't be stunt performers simply because we were women," recalled Teymouri, who now appears in successful Iranian productions and trains male stunt performers, reflecting changing views in Iran.
"Eventually, they placed their trust in us" on film sets, she said.
"Because they saw our work, accepted it and liked it," added Teymouri, who earns a living teaching gymnastics.
"In the past, our presence on set used to unsettle them."
- 'Afraid of everything' -
Teymouri has inspired others, including Mahisa Babayi-Parsa, a nine-year-old who insisted she was not "afraid at all" when carrying out stunts.
"I've been set on fire twice. I've jumped from heights, tumbled down stairs, and even been ejected from a car," she beamed.
The stunt crew, a tight-knit team of women and men, gathers for practice several times each month.
During rehearsals in which a woman is engulfed in flames, colleagues remain on standby with a fire extinguisher and a wet blanket, ready to intervene.
When a man prepares to be set alight for a bicycle stunt, women supervise the process, challenging established norms.
Mixed-gender participation remains banned in many sports in Iran, where men and women are not even permitted to visit the same gym.
"I'm someone who gets scared very easily: I'm afraid of heights and speed.
I'm afraid of everything," Teymouri said.
"But facing my fear gives me immense pleasure every time" and "that's what drove me to survive in this profession," she added, sporting sunglasses and a cap worn backwards. — AFP

Title: 521kg meth seized from jet in Laos declared as vape products to conceal drugs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 521kg of crystal methamphetamine seized from a private jet in Laos was declared as vape products in the aircraft's cargo manifest to conceal the illicit shipment bound for Manila.
The aircraft, which belongs to a Malaysian-operated aviation company, was intercepted by Lao authorities at Luang Prabang International Airport on Oct 1 before the drugs could be flown to the Philippines.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations revealed that the private jet initially departed Subang Airport without any cargo before arriving in Laos.
He said the drugs were believed to have been loaded onto the aircraft in Laos for onward transport to Manila.

Title: Filipino suspected of masterminding Laos crystal meth smuggling plot
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Filipino is believed to have masterminded an attempt to smuggle more than half a tonne of crystal methamphetamine from Laos to Manila on a private jet linked to a Malaysian-operated aviation company.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said preliminary investigations found that the individual had arranged to charter the aircraft for US$49,500 (RM202,250) to transport goods from Laos to the Philippines.
He said Malaysian police had shared information about the individual with the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency to help trace and arrest the suspect.

Title: Haze worsens with 37 areas recording unhealthy API levels
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions are worsening, with the number of areas recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings rising from 36 to 37 today.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Seremban recorded the highest reading at 186, followed by Bukit Rambai and Bandaraya Melaka at 184.
Other affected areas include Nilai (183), Segamat (183), Johan Setia (183), Pasir Gudang (181), Tangkak (181) and Tasek Ipoh (178).
In the Klang Valley, Shah Alam recorded an API reading of 178.
In Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda recorded 171, while Cheras registered 170. Putrajaya also recorded an API reading of 170.
Other affected areas include Alor Gajah (178), Tanjung Malim (173), Rompin (170), Sungai Petani (157) and Seberang Perai (119).
The API categorises readings of zero to 50 as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and readings above 300 as hazardous.

Title: New York City man shot by ICE agents with child in car
Article:
NEW YORK: US immigration agents shot and wounded a man on Thursday while he was in his car with a child in the Marble Hill neighbourhood of New York City, according to the mayor, city police and eyewitnesses.
"Early reports indicate agents surrounded (the man) and a 5-year-old child in his car before firing multiple rounds," New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement.
The mayor said the child was believed to have been physically unharmed.
"This is an unconscionable and incredibly serious situation," Mamdani said, adding that he planned to speak to President Donald Trump and "demand that he ends all ICE enforcement actions in our city. I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorise our communities."
The Department of Homeland Security, ICE's parent agency, said in a statement that ICE officers were conducting a "targeted enforcement operation" in the Bronx, New York, to arrest a man from the Dominican Republic with a prior criminal conviction.
"During the incident, an ICE officer discharged his weapon and the criminal illegal alien was injured," DHS said, adding that ICE officers rendered immediate aid. "The individual is alive and at a local hospital."
The shooting occurred at around 4pm ET (2000 GMT), DHS said.
Pedro Almarez, who works at a restaurant near the scene, said he heard shots fired and went outside to see several officers wearing ICE attire.
"There were a lot of ICE officers, three or four cars," Almarez told Reuters by phone, adding that the man who was shot appeared to be between 20 and 30 years old.
He said NYPD officers arrived about 10 minutes later. The man was only removed from his car after an ambulance arrived, he said.
At the scene, where police strung yellow crime-scene tape to cordon off a city block, a woman standing on a balcony overlooking the area told officers they were "taking our children", according to a Reuters witness.
Federal immigration agents have shot at least 21 people since Republican President Donald Trump returned to office, seven fatally, sparking protests across the US.
Critics contend that Trump's push to ramp up deportations has led to an increasing number of violent confrontations and accuse the administration of resisting accountability for the agents involved.

Title: Asia races to stockpile oil, speed up renewables in response to Iran war
Article:
ASIAN countries are racing to raise their oil stockpiling capacity, complete a regional power grid and speed up renewables in response to supply risks laid bare by the Iran war.
Southeast Asia has been worst hit by the energy impact as 80 per cent of the oil transported through the Strait of Hormuz from the Gulf flowed to the region before the Iran war began.
"The most advanced efforts are support for the development of oil stockpiling systems in each country and regional joint stockpiling on (a) voluntary basis," nine Southeast Asian nations said in a joint statement issued along with Japan and Australia.
Japan agreed on action plans with its Asian partners to boost crude oil reserves across the region following a meeting of the Japan-led Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC), a Japanese state minister on trade said on Thursday.
After a separate session with Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, Japan's State Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry Takagi Kei said they had expressed a willingness to cooperate to strengthen Asia's oil stockpiling capacity.
Philippines, which imports nearly all of its oil and fuel, will create a national reserve by the end of 2027, its energy secretary, Sharon Garin said on Thursday, adding that it could subsequently be converted into a regional stockpile.
The Southeast Asian archipelago is the chair of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) this year.
Garin said countries will decide if they want to host a regional oil stockpile, and also the terms of sale that should be determined by the country itself.
"In the Philippines, what we want is if there's any country that wants to store the crude or their petroleum products here. In case of any emergency the country gets priority on this on the stocks," she said.
The Asean member countries also pledged to increase the share of clean energy in power generation, targeting 30 per cent renewables in total primary energy supply and 45 per cent in installed power capacity.
The region is among the biggest laggards in green energy.
Renewables make up 14.1 per cent of primary energy, well short of a 2025 target of 25 per cent, while green power has made up 33.7 per cent of total capacity since 2020 against a 2025 target of 35 per cent, the ninth Asean energy outlook showed this week.
The countries also reached an enhanced preliminary agreement on developing a long-delayed regional power grid, which Garin called a landmark accomplishment.
The concept of a regional electricity network was first announced in December 1997.
"The first study was to connect with 2045, and that's too far because that's 20 years. So they're reviewing again to make it a faster implementation," Garin said.

Title: Nvidia-backed Firmus scraps US$5bil Australian IPO on poor demand
Article:
SYDNEY: Australia's Firmus, a data centre operator backed by Nvidia, shelved its US$5 billion initial public offering, citing market volatility and conditions, and said it would opt for a private fundraising round instead.
Firmus' IPO would have been the second-largest new share sale in Australia's history but met lukewarm demand, a warning sign that investors remain selective about AI issuers even as the artificial intelligence boom drives global markets.
"Firmus will now pursue capital from the private markets and consider alternative public and private market options," Firmus said in a statement, adding the terms did not correctly reflect the strength of its business and long-term growth outlook.
"The board therefore concluded that proceeding with the offer was not in the best interests of the company and its shareholders," it said.
The company initially planned to sell its shares at AUS$11 each, giving Firmus an equity valuation of US$30.6 billion, nearly triple the US$10.5 billion valuation it achieved following a fundraising round at the start of August.
Firmus, backed by major AI companies and investors Nvidia and Coatue Management, along with Blackstone and Jane Street, designs and operates ​modular AI factories using proprietary energy and cooling technology.
It currently has two leased online data centres in Melbourne and Singapore and plans to build five more across the Asia-Pacific. Its draft prospectus said it would make US$5 billion in annual earnings within five years from the data centres.
Firmus' valuation jump made investors wary, given the company had only two centres operating and had no track record of building any AI data centres.
"They were asking for a very big price tag for what would likely be expected to happen in the future assuming near flawless execution," said Joseph Koh, a portfolio manager at Blackwattle Investment Partners, who looked at the Firmus IPO but did not bid for stock.
"And so I think the market wasn't comfortable taking that leap of faith quite at this stage yet," he said.
With debt of about US$30 billion, according to analysts working for the IPO's joint lead managers, the company founded in 2019 would have had an enterprise value of US$60 billion, more than some of Australia's longest-established companies.
Fund manager Ten Cap's co-founder Jun Bei Liu said the pulled Firmus deal showed a broader shift was taking place in which investors were becoming more focused on the economics of AI investments and converting infrastructure spending into returns.
"I think the Firmus situation represents an important reality check for the AI investment boom, but I wouldn't interpret it as the beginning of the end of the AI trade," Liu said.
"There are certainly Firmus-specific issues, particularly around the speed of its valuation increase, the enormous capital requirements and the execution risks associated with delivering its ambitious expansion plans."
VALUATION WORRIES
The world's largest technology companies, including Nvidia and SpaceX, are still busy tapping debt markets for tens of billions of dollars, while Anthropic is seeking to raise as much as US$100 billion in an IPO.
But in the latest sign of investors' concerns about returns from AI, US-listed chipmakers, which have soared over 80 per cent so far this year, fell 3.4 per cent on Thursday in the wake of a report from the Financial Times that OpenAI's annualised revenue was US$20 billion less than the company previously signalled.
Firmus' term sheet sent out when the deal launched had said indicative offers for the IPO were already enough to cover the transaction. Investors started to pull those orders on Wednesday as they began to lose confidence in the deal, one person involved in the transaction said. The person could not be named discussing information that was not public.
Investors had grown more wary after being told on Tuesday about escrow arrangements that would have allowed more than half the stock to be sold by existing investors from day one. That sparked worries existing investors could sell huge amounts of shares, potentially hurting Firmus' early trading performance.
The company considered cutting the price of the shares to entice more investors to place orders, the person said, but opted instead to look towards a private funding round.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mexico prison brawl leaves 10 dead
Article:
MAZATLAN: Ten people were killed and more than a dozen injured after a fight broke out at a prison in Mexico's Sinaloa state on Thursday, the local government said.
The Sinaloa Public Security Secretariat said on X that "a brawl occurred inside the prison facilities", without providing further details on what led to the violence.
A surge of security forces was able to restore control, with an AFP reporter witnessing the arrival of an armoured vehicle and ambulances.
Sinaloa's Secretary of Public Security, Sinuhe Tellez, said in a video posted on social media that "nine inmates and a minor who was visiting lost their lives, and 16 inmates were injured".
Sinaloa state in north-western Mexico has become a battleground for warring factions of the Sinaloa drug-trafficking cartel.
It is one of six Mexican states that the US State Department advises Americans not to travel to due to security concerns.

Title: Euro skids toward fifth weekly fall but selling pressure slows
Article:
SINGAPORE: The euro was headed for a fifth straight weekly drop on Friday, though there were signs the selling streak was losing momentum as France's tumbling debt market stabilised and a decline in US yields took some steam out of the dollar's rally.
The common currency had hit a 17-month low of US$1.1161 on Monday on market worries about France's record high debt load and the difficult political path to budget cuts, in contrast with a robust-looking US dollar and US economy.
It has since recovered to trade at US$1.1211, for a fall this week of 0.3 per cent and a five-week drop of more than three per cent on the dollar.
The euro/sterling cross is also down 0.3 per cent on the week to trade near a 16-month low at 84.74 pence. The euro/Swiss cross has steadied around 0.9324 francs per euro after notching last week its biggest weekly fall in 17 months.
"My take is all the moves are pretty stretched," said Matt Simpson, senior analyst at StoneX in Brisbane.
"You probably only get two or three big moves a year on the euro and this has been one of them... but bearish momentum is waning (and) I'd tread really carefully at these lows."
France's far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen presented plans this week to cut the budget deficit, which markets took as reassuring given hard-left rival Jean-Luc Melenchon has asked the central bank to cancel government debts.
French students blockaded high schools and marched through cities on Thursday in the latest wave of protests about education conditions, highlighting the tricky balance for leaders between demand for social spending and leery markets.
"France's bond sell-off and the social unrest are now operating in a feedback loop," said Macquarie strategists Thierry Wizman and Gareth Berry in a note to clients.
"An intensification of the street riots could lead to higher bond yield spreads."
Elsewhere, the dollar's moves were small and gains slowed as US yields headed for their biggest weekly drop in about three months, with the market rallying strongly overnight.
The yen headed for a fourth straight weekly drop, though moves in the last three of those weeks have been very small as it has steadied around 158 yen to the dollar.
Vishnu Varathan, head of Asia-Pacific macro strategy at Mizuho Securities in Singapore, said the dollar sat in a "precarious pole position, flattered by a dismal euro and yen."
The Australian dollar hovered at US$0.6960 and sterling at US$1.3233.
The New Zealand dollar is on its longest losing streak in more than four years, as it heads for a seventh straight weekly decline thanks to how low New Zealand interest rates are — at 2.75 per cent — compared with a Fed funds rate between 3.75 per cent and 4 per cent.
The kiwi sat at US$0.5601 and is not far from breaking its 2025 low of US$0.5485.

Title: Gold rises on softer dollar, easing yields; Fed outlook in focus
Article:
BENGALURU: Gold firmed on Friday as a softer US dollar and easing Treasury yields boosted bullion's appeal, while market players weighed lingering inflation concerns and the outlook for Federal Reserve interest rates.
Spot gold rose 0.9 per cent to US$4,169.32 per ounce by 0137 GMT after hitting a two-month low on Wednesday. US gold futures gained 0.9 per cent to US$4,194.40.
The dollar rally took a breather, making greenback-priced bullion more affordable for holders of other currencies, while the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield slipped for a second straight session.
"Possible tightening later on could keep gold at risk, especially as inflation fears remain high amid a rise in oil prices following increased Middle East supply disruption risks. However, ongoing central bank demand may limit losses," said Tony Sage, CEO of Critical Metals.
"Looking ahead, traders will watch upcoming economic data that could provide further monetary policy clues and influence sentiment ahead of the Federal Reserve's October meeting."
Last month, the US central bank voted unanimously to raise the policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point.
St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the US central bank will need to hike rates again to bring inflation back to its 2 per cent target, although he declined to say what policymakers should do at their meeting later this month.
Traders are pricing in an 18 per cent chance of a rate hike in October and an 82 per cent probability of an increase in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
Gold is traditionally seen as a hedge against inflation, but higher interest rates diminish the appeal of the non-yielding asset.
President Donald Trump said the US will not launch an attack on Iran before November's US midterm congressional elections, asserting that the two countries are having "productive" talks about ending the six-month-old war.
Spot silver rose 1.1 per cent to US$60.00, platinum gained 2.2 per cent to US$1,670.15 and palladium climbed 2.1 per cent to US$1,146.98. But all three metals were on track for weekly losses.

Title: Japan's Nikkei falls as AI doubts, bond stress weigh
Article:
TOKYO: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell sharply on Friday as doubts about the red-hot AI sector emerged and stress in global bond markets weighed on sentiment.
The Nikkei 225 slid 1.06 per cent to 68,308.92 in early trading, poised for a slight weekly decline. The broader Topix slipped 0.24 per cent to 4,081.62.
US equity indexes fell overnight, dragged lower by technology companies after a Financial Times report said OpenAI's annualized revenue was US$20 billion less than the company previously signalled. Euro zone borrowing costs remained elevated as a surge in oil prices intensified inflation, and concerns lingered over France's budget.
"Reports that a major unlisted AI company's revenue fell short of its own forecasts triggered a chain reaction of selling in related stocks, and the sharp rise in crude oil prices also appeared to have an impact," Sony Financial Group analysts said in a report. "Globally high interest rates, driven in part by concerns over France's fiscal situation, are also capping stock price gains."
Data on Friday showed Japan's August household spending fell 3.1 per cent year-on-year, underscoring cautious consumer sentiment and persistent inflation pressures. The Bank of Japan on Thursday noted cost-driven price increases spreading to consumer goods, signalling a meaningful chance of further rate hikes this year.
There were 112 advancers on the Nikkei 225, outweighing 110 decliners, with 3 unchanged.
The largest loser on the Nikkei was SoftBank Group, a major investor in OpenAI, which sank 5.40 per cent and dragged on the index. Furukawa Electric fell 4.83 per cent, followed by Murata Manufacturing, which lost 4.68 per cent.
The index's largest percentage gainers were Nomura Research Institute, up 5.13 per cent, followed by Baycurrent, up 3.97 per cent, and Shift, up 3.92 per cent.

Title: Tech stocks struggle on AI spending worries, elevated yields
Article:
SINGAPORE: Asian stocks slipped on Friday and were poised for a second straight weekly drop as investors fretted about elevated energy prices, bond market ructions and the huge sums needed to fund AI investment.
Brent crude futures were at US$103.70 per barrel in Asian hours after surging more than 4 per cent in the previous session on concerns over the war in the Middle East that has fanned inflation worries and led to higher rates across the globe.
President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the US will not launch an attack on Iran before November's US midterm elections, although traders remained sceptical of any progress being made to end the war.
"The big question for markets is whether Trump sticks to his word if Iranian attacks intensify," said Nick Twidale, chief market strategist at ATFX Global.
"Any indication that the White House is reconsidering military action could see oil prices spike sharply higher, particularly with tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz already under significant pressure."
In stocks, MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was down 0.16 per cent, set for an over 1 per cent drop for the week. Markets in South Korea and Taiwan were closed for a holiday. Japan's Nikkei fell more than 1 per cent.
Tech stocks led Wall Street's main indexes lower overnight after a report that OpenAI's annualised revenue was US$20 billion less than the company previously signalled hit sentiment.
"It has been a sea of red across technology, AI infrastructure and semiconductors, with the OpenAI headlines seemingly providing the catalyst for investors to take some exposure off the table," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone.
"For now, though, the price action suggests investors are becoming more selective about where they want exposure and, importantly, what price they are prepared to pay for future growth," he said in a note.
BOND BINGE FOR AI
Investors were also weighing a massive round of fundraising that appears to be on the way, with SpaceX, Broadcom and Oracle all expected to raise billions to buy high-end AI chips.
Australia's Firmus, a data centre operator backed by Nvidia , shelved its US$5 billion initial public offering, citing market volatility and conditions, and said it would opt for a private fundraising round instead.
A toxic mix of higher energy costs, expectations of central bank interest rate hikes and concerns over rising government debts have fuelled a months-long global bond selloff, pushing borrowing costs to multi-decade highs.
"With long-term yields back around multi-decade highs, investors no longer have the luxury of valuing AI growth in a low-cost-of-capital world," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo.
Chanana said higher sovereign yields and now rising corporate issuance to fund AI infrastructure mean capital is becoming "both more expensive and more selective, which puts balance sheets and the quality of future earnings firmly in focus."
FOCUS REMAINS ON FRANCE
France has been hit particularly hard as investors scrutinise its debt load, budget deficit and political outlook ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
"With the two rounds of the presidential elections only in April and May next year, French bond spreads are still looking at more than half a year of higher volatility and continued spread elevation," ING analysts said in a note.
US Treasury markets have been calmer as solid auctions this week helped the mood somewhat. The benchmark 10-year yield was steady at 5.226 per cent but was not far from the 24-year high it hit on Wednesday.
"It does not mean the bond market sell-off is over, but it does at least put it on pause, at least just for now," ING analysts said.
In currencies, the dollar stood tall as the euro was set for a fifth straight week in the red. It last fetched US$1.122, straddling the 17-month low it touched earlier this week on French debt worries.

Title: 2027 Budget to ensure national progress benefits all, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget  reaffirms the government's commitment to ensuring that national progress benefits all Malaysians through continued improvements in their standard of living, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
In a post on X, Anwar said the fifth Madani Budget also prioritised the people's well-being and their ability to live with dignity.
"Insya-Allah, I will table the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat this afternoon, with the aspiration to 'reach for the skies while remaining rooted to the earth'," he said.
He urged the public to watch the live tabling of the 2027 Budget on major television channels and digital platforms at 3.30pm today.

Title: Egypt president to make two-day state visit to Malaysia from Oct 9
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Egypt President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi will undertake a two-day state visit to Malaysia starting today at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
The Foreign Ministry said the president will be accompanied by Cabinet ministers and senior government officials for his first state visit to Malaysia since assuming office in June 2014.
"Malaysia and Egypt established diplomatic relations in 1959. Both countries have since maintained warm and cordial relations through robust cooperation at both the bilateral and multilateral levels.
"The state visit by President El-Sisi is expected to further strengthen this longstanding partnership through the elevation of bilateral relations to a Strategic Partnership," the ministry said in a statement.
El-Sisi will receive a state welcoming ceremony followed by an audience with Sultan Ibrahim at Istana Negara, where His Majesty will host a state banquet in honour of the president and his delegation.
The ministry said El-Sisi is also scheduled to meet Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to assess progress in bilateral cooperation and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest.
Both leaders will witness the exchange of memoranda of understanding between Malaysia and Egypt, followed by an official high tea at the Seri Perdana Complex hosted by the prime minister.
In 2025, Egypt was Malaysia's seventh largest trading partner in Africa.
Malaysia's total trade with Egypt was valued at RM3.08 billion (US$0.72 billion), with exports at RM2.55 billion (US$0.60 billion) and imports at RM0.53 billion (US$0.12 billion).
From January to August, total trade between the two countries increased by 74.7 per cent to RM3.49 billion (US$0.87 billion).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Father recalls heartbreaking scene of daughter, grandchildren's fatal crash
Article:
TANJONG KARANG: A father is struggling to come to terms with the loss of his eldest daughter and two grandchildren in a road crash involving a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) and a lorry at Bukit Talang, Jalan Raja Musa, yesterday.
Mat Talpi Salamat, 72, said he rushed to the scene after receiving a call from his fifth child, Norhaslinda, 34, informing him that his eldest daughter, Norawalysa, 44, had been involved in the crash at about 1.30pm.
The grocery store owner arrived to find his grandchildren, Auni Syazana Suhaimi, 12, and Ahmad Syah Fawwaz Suhaimi, 8, lying at the scene, while firefighters worked to free Norawalysa, who was trapped in the vehicle.
Another grandchild, Ahmad Syah Fitri, 10, who was also in the MPV, sustained head injuries.
Recalling the tragedy at Masjid Darul Iman in Kampung Parit Serong last night, Mat Talpi fought back tears as he described seeing his grandchildren at the scene.
"When I arrived, I saw my grandchildren lying there, while firefighters were extricating their mother.
"Seeing that there was no hope, I kissed them right there. How can I forget them when they loved me so much?" he said.
Mat Talpi said he had last seen Norawalysa and her family the previous week, when they shared a meal of fried noodles prepared by her.
"I never imagined she and her children would leave us like this. She was my eldest child and an exemplary sibling. She was friendly and always willing to help. It is hard for our family to accept this trial," he said.
Norhaslinda said she noticed a change in her sister's demeanour during the family gathering the previous week.
"She usually talked a lot, but that day she was mostly silent. Only after she passed away did I realise it was a sign she would be leaving us forever," she said.
Norhaslinda said her sister had helped her greatly, particularly with career guidance and financial support.
"We accept her passing," she said.
Norawalysa and her two children were buried in a single grave at the Kampung Parit Serong Islamic Cemetery at 1am today.
The three died after their Proton Exora MPV crashed into the rear of a lorry yesterday afternoon.
Initial police
investigations
found that the lorry had pulled over onto the left shoulder of the road due to a flat tyre.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: [UPDATED] Malaysia retains Tier 2 ranking in US human trafficking report for third year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has retained its Tier 2 ranking in the 2026 Trafficking in Persons Report released by the United States Department of State, marking the third consecutive year it has held the rating.
The Home Ministry said the ranking reflected continued international recognition of Malaysia's sustained efforts to combat human trafficking.
The report acknowledged the country's progress, including stronger law enforcement, prosecutions of public officials complicit in trafficking crimes and increased government funding for anti-trafficking operations.
Other measures included a significant increase in specialised officers, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak, and amendments to two regulations under the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 to improve the duration of permissions granted under the law.
The ministry also cited related amendments concerning extended protection orders and the management of victims whose extended protection orders had expired, as well as the opening of new shelters operated by non-governmental organisations.
Enforcement capacity in Sabah and Sarawak had also been strengthened, with operations targeting high-risk sectors such as oil palm plantations and rubber glove manufacturing, it said in a statement today.
Malaysia retained its Tier 2 ranking in the 2025 report after receiving the same rating in 2024.
In 2023, the country was placed on the Tier 2 Watch List, with its last Tier 2 rating before 2024 in 2017.
The ministry said the 2026 report also outlined eight recommendations for Malaysia to implement during the next assessment period, from April 1 this year to March 31 next year.
Among the key recommendations were strengthening early victim identification mechanisms, improving the quality of case investigations, eliminating recruitment fees charged to workers and expanding strategic partnerships with NGOs.
In response, the government has outlined several strategies, including strengthening the integrity of public servants and establishing a victim management system in line with international standards.
The ministry said the government would also strengthen cooperation with civil society organisations and NGOs, while making greater use of digital technology and artificial intelligence.
The ministry added that the Council for Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants (MAPO), which it leads alongside other government agencies, was committed to implementing coordinated measures to address emerging trends, including job scams.
Combating human trafficking requires close cooperation among various parties through a holistic approach centred on enforcement and legislation, victim protection and prevention, it said.
"The government is confident that this comprehensive approach would strengthen efforts to combat human trafficking, bring offenders to justice, uphold human rights and protect victims, while safeguarding public order and national security."

Title: PTPTN borrowers can negotiate loan restructuring, deferment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Borrowers struggling to repay their National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loans can negotiate a repayment restructuring or apply for a deferment.
The Higher Education Ministry said the government recognised the financial difficulties faced by borrowers genuinely struggling to settle their debts.
"As of Aug 31, 2026, PTPTN's loan repayment arrears stood at RM10.7 billion, involving 1.16 million borrowers," the ministry said in a written parliamentary reply.
This was in response to Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson), who asked for the latest figures on PTPTN debt and the number of borrowers in arrears.
The ministry said initiatives were ongoing to ensure PTPTN's long-term financial sustainability, including refining loan terms and conditions to better target assistance based on the agency's capacity.
It added that repayment collection would be strengthened through enforcement and strategic cooperation with government and corporate agencies.

Title: Selangor religious schools closed due to haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All religious schools under the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) will close from today due to the haze.
Its director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad said the closure was in line with an announcement by the Education Ministry.

schools in four states
, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as Rompin district in Pahang, would be closed due to deteriorating haze conditions.

Title: 12 politicians involved in 19 cases granted DNAA since 2010
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nineteen cases involving 12 politicians were granted a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) in the High Court and lower courts nationwide between 2010 and July this year.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the figures were based on information from the Office of the Chief Registrar of the Federal Court and a review of criminal case records.
She said, unlike civil cases, criminal cases were not subject to a limitation period, meaning individuals granted a DNAA could still be charged again with the same offences.
"This procedure may be undertaken if the prosecution decides to do so, based on the facts, evidence and developments in the case," she said in a written parliamentary reply published on the Parliament website.
She was responding to Pang Hok Liong (PH-Labis), who asked about the number of criminal cases involving politicians and high-profile leaders that had been granted a DNAA.
Azalina said details of specific cases could be obtained directly from the Attorney-General's Chambers, which holds the relevant prosecution records and information.
She clarified that a DNAA did not amount to an acquittal.

Title: Haze: Penang schools remain open, outdoor activities suspended
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang schools will continue operating as usual, but all outdoor activities must be postponed amid the haze, said the state Education Department.
The department said it was monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings around the clock across four stations in Minden, Seberang Jaya, Seberang Prai, and Balik Pulau.
As of 9.55pm, the average API reading had dropped by 4.5 points from 129 to 124.5.
In a Facebook statement, the department said it took the royal decree of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia on safeguarding the health and welfare of students and school personnel.
"For now, schools in Penang will continue to operate as usual based on current API readings. However, all outdoor activities must be postponed," it said.
The department said these measures aligned with the Education Ministry's directive issued yesterday.
It added that educational institutions must act if haze conditions reach or exceed guidelines, including modifying, postponing, or cancelling outdoor activities.
The department urged parents to monitor their children's health and stay updated via official ministry, department, and school channels.
"Close cooperation between schools and parents is essential to safeguarding students' welfare throughout the haze episode," it added.
The King had advised that schools in areas with prolonged API readings between 150 and 180 be closed due to worsening conditions.
Last night, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said schools in four states, including one district in Pahang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, would
close today
due to worsening haze.

Title: RM3,100 salary for singles in KL — baseline or comfortable?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A monthly salary of about RM3,100 for a single person in Kuala Lumpur should be seen as a financial baseline for a reasonable standard of living, not a guarantee of financial comfort.
Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) Faculty of Human Ecology dean and personal financial planning lecturer Prof Dr Mohamad Fazli Sabri said the figure could serve as a benchmark for assessing whether a person could meet basic needs while setting aside some savings and preparing for emergencies.
Fazli said income adequacy should not be measured solely by one's ability to pay for food, rent and transport, but should also account for healthcare, communication, social participation, savings and protection against financial shocks.
"Minimum wage is the lowest wage set through policy and legislation. A living wage addresses a broader question: after working full-time, does a person earn enough to live reasonably?
"This includes having some savings and financial protection, rather than merely having enough to get by until the end of the month," he told Berita Harian.
It was previously reported that a single person living in Kuala Lumpur was estimated to need a living wage of about RM3,100 a month to maintain a reasonable standard of living.
The estimate was based on the 2026 Government-Linked Enterprises Activation and Reform Programme (GEAR-uP) initiative, which accounted for changes in the cost of living.
Fazli said RM3,100 was a reasonable starting point, but it was too early to consider it a comfortable salary, as financial well-being depended largely on individual commitments and spending habits.
"Someone who rents a room near their workplace and uses public transport would have a different financial position from someone who owns a car, pays a loan, rents a place alone and supports their parents," he said.
He said it was therefore wrong to assume that every single person earning RM3,100 automatically enjoyed financial well-being.
Differences in transport costs also illustrated how lifestyle choices could affect income adequacy, particularly in urban areas.
Citing the Belanjawanku 2024/2025 guide, he said estimated monthly expenses for a single person in the Klang Valley stood at about RM1,970 for public transport users, compared with RM2,800 for car owners.
"This difference shows that transport choices alone can have a significant impact on a person's financial position," he said.
Fazli said the financial margin would shrink further for those with commitments such as National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loans, insurance or takaful payments, parental support and emergency savings.
"For example, someone earning RM3,100 may be able to pay all their bills, but if only RM50 or RM100 remains after meeting all their commitments, a minor emergency, such as a car breakdown or illness, could force them to use a credit card, buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) services or borrow from family," he said.

Title: #NSTviral: F1 race over, but memories linger; Sepang clips captivate fans
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The race is long over, but Malaysian fans are still reliving Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia through "cinematic video clips" of cars speeding past Sepang's grandstands against an orange sunset.
Videos circulating on Threads capture the evening
atmosphere at Sepang International Circuit,
with the fading sunlight and haze lending the event a movie-like quality.
One video posted by user @mxrul drew more than 42,500 likes and 311,000 views.

User @saifuddinsuhaimy, whose video drew 638,000 views and 68,500 likes, wrote: "This is the most beautiful and priceless scene in F1, with the sunset as a backdrop. Hopefully, we'll meet again at Sepang."
Amid fans sharing their memories, some also called for a permanent return of F1 to Sepang.
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the Oct 4 race, ahead of Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and Ferrari's Hamilton.

Malaysia's return to the F1
calendar.

Title: Ringgit opens marginally higher against US dollar as 2027 Budget fiscal outlook in focus
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened marginally higher against the US dollar on Friday, with markets remaining cautious as they continued to assess the fiscal outlook ahead of the tabling of the 2027 Budget.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said markets would focus on the government's fiscal position, with expectations that it would maintain fiscal discipline and keep the fiscal deficit on a downward trajectory.

It fell against the euro to 4.5839/5912 from 4.5719/5775 at Thursday's close, weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5862/5905 from 2.5834/5867, and eased against the British pound to 5.4076/4162 from 5.3930/3996.

Title: RTD uncovers fake international driving permits with bogus online verification system
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Fake International Driving Permits (IDPs) sold to foreigners for up to RM500 have come under scrutiny after authorities uncovered documents linked to websites designed to make them appear legitimate.
The questionable permits, purportedly valid for up to five years, were detected and seized during enforcement operations targeting foreign motorists in the capital.
Checks on one document revealed a website where its serial number could be verified, creating the impression of an official verification system.
The website is believed to have been set up by the syndicate behind the fake permits to mislead motorists and enforcement personnel.
Kuala Lumpur Road Transport Department (RTD) director Hamidi Adam said the department had detected parties offering documents purported to be IDPs to foreigners despite doubts over their validity under Malaysian law.
"We have detected parties offering documents claimed to be International Driving Permits to foreigners for fees of up to RM500, with purported validity periods of up to five years.
"These documents do not meet the recognition requirements for legal driving in Malaysia," he said in a statement.
Hamidi said foreigners who purchased the documents could mistakenly believe they were legally entitled to drive in Malaysia.
He stressed that merely possessing a document bearing the words "International Driving Permit" did not automatically entitle its holder to drive on Malaysian roads.
"Such documents must be issued by the relevant authorities or parties authorised by the country concerned and must fulfil the recognition requirements applicable in Malaysia," he said.
Hamidi pointed out that IDPs issued by Malaysia's RTD were valid for only one year under the Convention on Road Traffic signed in Geneva on Sept 19, 1949.
He said the use of such permits was also subject to the laws and regulations of the respective countries or territories.
The discovery of the questionable documents and their accompanying verification website has highlighted concerns over how easily foreign motorists and enforcement personnel could be misled by documents designed to resemble legitimate international driving credentials.
Although a serial number may appear on a website, this does not necessarily mean the document is recognised by the Malaysian authorities or that its holder is legally permitted to drive in the country.
Hamidi urged foreigners not to be deceived by individuals or organisations offering international driving documents without proper authority or recognition.
"The RTD will not compromise on the use of invalid driving documents. Appropriate enforcement action will be taken against anyone found violating the law," he said.
The discovery comes as Kuala Lumpur RTD intensifies enforcement against foreign motorists through its Ops Pewa.
During yesterday's operation, officers seized 47 of the 121 vehicles inspected, comprising 40 motorcycles, four cars and three goods vehicles.
A total of 273 notices were issued under the Road Transport Act 1987 for offences including driving licence violations, expired motor vehicle licences, insurance breaches and technical infringements.
The
operation
also saw 58 foreigners, including drivers, pillion riders and vehicle attendants, referred to the Immigration Department for further action.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shares slip as oil jumps and bond yields stay high
Article:
BOSTON/LONDON/SYDNEY: Global shares slid on Thursday as a mild pullback in sovereign bond yields was countered by a jump in oil prices and indicators of the massive debt that technology companies may need to sustain their dramatic artificial intelligence-fueled growth.
Wall Street's main indexes fell, with the S&P 500 down about 0.5 per cent and the Nasdaq off nearly 1.3 per cent. Chipmakers, which have soared over 80 per cent so far this year, were clear underperformers on the day following a report that OpenAI's annualized revenues were US$20 billion less than the company previously signaled.
Euro zone borrowing costs rose on Thursday as the surge in oil prices intensified inflation concerns, though investors took a breather from selling bonds of heavily indebted countries such as France and Italy. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes , also pulled back from its elevated levels, dipping 5 basis points to 5.227 per cent. Yields started moving lower after a 30-year bond auction met with solid demand, showing investors remain willing to buy long-dated government debt, despite the ongoing market selloff.
"Markets are going to be watchful if that contagion continues," said Kiran Ganesh, a multi-asset strategist at UBS Global Wealth Management.
"At this stage, the markets would be most comforted by monetary intervention," he added, referring to the ECB buying bonds to ease the market strains.
The pan-European STOXX 600 fell 0.75 per cent to around its lowest since June, while France's CAC-40 dropped 0.5 per cent, nearing its lows for the year in March.
Overnight in Asia, Japan's Nikkei had shed 1.4 per cent and South Korea's chipmaker-heavy KOSPI slumped 2.6 per cent.
AI DEBT RUSH
In commodity markets, oil prices settled 4 per cent higher, with Brent crude futures at US$104.28, on revived concerns about the war in the Middle East and growing supply disruptions due to a hurricane approaching the US Gulf Coast.
The US quarterly earnings season picks up pace next week with big banks, including JPMorgan, set to report results.
Optimism around strong earnings has buoyed US stocks lately despite shaky geopolitical developments and concerns about rising interest rates. The tech and energy sectors are expected to report the biggest quarterly earnings growth, while the broader S&P 500 is expected to post a punchy 30.6 per cent increase in quarterly earnings, according to LSEG data.
Vlad Barbalat, Liberty Mutual Group's chief investment officer and president of global risk & capital solutions, said the S&P 500's roughly 15 per cent return this year looks ordinary on the surface, but the composition is striking.
"The index has risen even as its forward P/E has fallen from roughly 22x to 19x, supported by exceptionally strong growth in rolling forward earnings, all while more than a third of S&P 500 stocks are down," Barbalat wrote in an email. "The result is a historically uncommon combination: a narrow rally in which the market has gotten cheaper even as the index hovers near all-time highs."
Debt remains a strong underwater current. The Wall Street Journal added to media reports on Wednesday that SpaceX , Broadcom and Oracle were all looking to raise serious money to buy high-end AI chips.
Broadcom was looking for US$50 billion in financing, while SpaceX was planning to issue US$30 billion in investment-grade debt and raise US$10 billion in loans to buy chips from Nvidia , which is a major shareholder in SpaceX. Credit default insurance on SpaceX jumped to record highs, while its shares and bonds lost ground.
SOVEREIGN BONDS VS CORPORATE DEBT
Still, the fact much of this money will be spent on AI equipment is set to be positive for earnings in the semiconductor and memory sectors.
Samsung Electronics on Thursday reported a 783 per cent jump in third-quarter operating profit to 107.4 trillion won (US$80.17 billion), though its shares lost 2.4 per cent.
TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, also reported a record third-quarter revenue of TUS$1.49 trillion (US$46.71 billion), up 50 per cent from the year-earlier period. Its shares fell 1.35 per cent.
All this corporate debt is coming at a time when sovereign bond markets are being sorely tested by inflation fears, ever-widening budget deficits and rising cash rates.
Minutes of the Federal Reserve's last meeting released on Wednesday showed "most" members considered another rate hike likely by year-end, though they would approach each meeting with an open mind.
Markets imply just a 17 per cent chance the Fed will move again this month, but are nearly 83 per cent priced for a rise in December.
"We expect a second Fed hike in December, though we see a strong chance the Fed ultimately concludes further tightening is unnecessary," analysts at Goldman Sachs wrote in a note.
Strains in the French bond market led Bank of France head Emmanuel Moulin to say the country's economic situation was serious on Wednesday, but he said it did not need help from the European Central Bank.
Still, the euro gained against the dollar as a rise in euro zone bond yields stalled. The greenback also retreated versus the yen, with the Japanese currency protected by the threat of intervention.
Non-interest-bearing gold has suffered as yields climbed, but it was steady at US$4,111 an ounce having found bids at two-month lows.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hurricane Isaias strengthens to Cat 2 en route to southern US
Article:
MIAMI: Hurricane Isaias intensified to Category 2 in the Gulf of Mexico's warm waters on Thursday as it churned towards the southern United States, the National Hurricane Centre (NHC) said.
The first hurricane of the Atlantic season, Isaias is forecast to make landfall in Florida, Alabama or Mississippi overnight from Friday to Saturday, according to the NHC.
It warned residents in the likely impact zone that emergency preparations to protect lives and property from high winds and storm surges "should be rushed to completion".
A storm surge warning, which signals the danger of life-threatening inundation, was in effect from the mouth of the Mississippi River to the Suwannee River, while a hurricane warning was in effect from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to the Gulf County line in Florida, the NHC said in its latest update.
Isaias, which was about 525km south of the Mississippi River delta, was packing maximum sustained winds of 155kph, making it a Category 2 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale.
Isaias comes unusually late as the first hurricane of the Atlantic season, which began on June 1.
The Pacific has already seen several hurricanes, including Polo, which at one point reached the highest strength, Category 5.

Title: Anwar to table 2027 Budget at 3.30pm today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will table the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat at 3.30pm today.
The tabling marks the fifth budget under his Madani Government, anchored by a commitment to ensure high-value growth translates equitably into the people's well-being while strengthening national economic resilience.
It will be broadcast live on local television stations and social media platforms.
According to a pre-budget statement on the Finance Ministry website, the 2027 Budget builds on the foundation set by previous budgets.
As the second budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), it continues to pursue the three Madani Economy pillars: raising the growth ceiling, raising the living standards floor, and driving public administration governance reforms.
The Finance Ministry said Malaysia's economy remains resilient following bold structural reforms, including fiscal consolidation and targeted subsidy rationalisation, despite global geopolitical uncertainties and international supply chain disruptions.
The 2027 Budget outlines 10 key focuses, including narrowing regional disparities, easing living costs through targeted aid like Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Budi Madani, strengthening the gig worker social safety net, and preparing for an ageing population by 2030.
Attention will also go to basic services such as education and healthcare, technology-driven public sector transformation via Government Technology (GovTech), workers' welfare through dignified wages, empowering local entrepreneurs through the 'Made by Malaysia' initiative, and securing high-value investments in semiconductors and artificial intelligence (AI).
In a post on X yesterday, Anwar expressed hope that the 2027 Budget would strengthen economic resilience, ease living costs, expand opportunities, and ensure development benefits are shared equitably.
According to the Parliament portal calendar, the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 will be debated at the policy stage for eight days starting next week.
Ministerial winding-up speeches are scheduled from Oct 26 to 29, followed by the committee stage debate from Nov 2 to 26 before the Bill is put to a vote in the Dewan Rakyat. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump says comment that Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles was misinterpreted
Article:
UNITED STATES: US President Donald Trump on Thursday said comments he made suggesting Iran could "take out" California cities had been misinterpreted, and that he was instead referring to the need for people to tolerate higher petrol prices.
Trump made the remarks at a political rally in Nebraska on Monday as he spoke about Americans' wartime economic sacrifices.
"Remember, with the war, it's just artificial, it's a little bit high, it's a small price to pay," he said then. "It's a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, for keeping our country safe. They could take out a city. Let 'em take out Los Angeles, let 'em take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and it's going to be over with very soon."
California's Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans quickly rebuked the remarks.
"What I was talking about was that a temporary increase in the price of Gasoline is a small price to pay for Iran not having a Nuclear Weapon," Trump said in a Truth Social post on Thursday.
"If you want to see a big price, can you imagine what it would be like if they bombed San Diego and/or Los Angeles?" he continued, saying he loved both cities.
Trump has previously shrugged off cost-of-living concerns stemming from the Iran conflict.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump administration to launch new vaccine research centre
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr., a vaccine sceptic, on Thursday announced a series of initiatives to study rare adverse effects of vaccines.
"We must listen to patients and families who report vaccine injuries – not dismiss or gaslight them," Kennedy said in a statement announcing the creation of a research centre dedicated to monitoring and addressing vaccine side effects.
Appointed by President Donald Trump despite lacking formal medical training, Kennedy has faced criticism from the World Health Organisation (WHO) and other medical experts for efforts to overhaul childhood vaccination in the United States.
Like all medicines, vaccines can have side effects, including mild ones such as a slight fever or pain at the injection site.
Serious adverse effects remain very rare and are subject to continuous monitoring by health officials to ensure that the benefits of vaccines outweigh the risks.
According to WHO, vaccination currently prevents up to five million deaths every year from diseases such as diphtheria, tetanus, influenza and measles.
"The issue really isn't whether we should study vaccine safety," epidemiologist Michael Osterholm, director of the University of Minnesota's Centre for Infectious Disease Research and Policy, told National Public Radio.
"Of course we should, but we already have systems in place that are constantly monitoring...to determine: Are there any adverse events associated with vaccination?"
Kennedy said the latest effort would help build a health system that "follows the evidence, and uses what we learn to make vaccines safer. This is how we earn back trust in our public health institutions."
The announcement comes as the federal health department has undergone significant budget cuts and the country faces its worst measles outbreak in 35 years.
The highly contagious illness has made a strong comeback in the US in recent years among unvaccinated populations, amid growing mistrust of health officials.
In the eastern US state of Pennsylvania, local authorities have reported five measles-related deaths in 2026 alone.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Remand extended: Teen suspect held six more days over murder of classmate Irene Sofiya in Yong Peng
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Oct 9 — The remand of a 16-year-old boy suspected of murdering a female student at a school in Yong Peng has been extended by six days, from tomorrow until Oct 15.
The extension was granted by Magistrate Aimi Nawwar Mohamad Othman at the Magistrate’s Court here today.
The teenager had previously been remanded for six days from Oct 4 to assist in the investigation into the death of Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16.
The Form Four student, who was the suspect’s classmate, was found unconscious and covered in blood in a school hall in Yong Peng at about 5.50pm on Oct 3. She was later pronounced dead.
Her body was sent to Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI) for a post-mortem examination.
Police have said the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
Irene Sofiya was buried at the Kampung Parit Arshad Muslim Cemetery last Sunday after the post-mortem was completed at HSNI. — Bernama

Title: ‘I didn’t attack Nhaveen’: Accused tells High Court fight started with blow to friend’s face
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 9 — One of the four men accused of murdering teenager T. Nhaveen nine years ago denied yesterday that he and the three other accused carried out an attack on the victim and his friend at Padang Openg following a scuffle on Jalan Kaki Bukit, Gelugor.
J. Ragesuthen, 27, told the High Court here that he was on Jalan Kaki Bukit when a “scuffle” occurred between his friend — who was another accused and a minor at the time of the incident — and T. Previin, who was Nhaveen’s friend.
He said Previin acted aggressively and struck his friend with a helmet, and that he stopped Previin from continuing to attack his friend, while two other friends who are also accused, S. Gokulan and another person, subsequently arrived to break up the fight.
“I saw Previin hit another accused friend in the face with a helmet, and he passed out at the scene. Suddenly, Belang (their friend) came to the scene on a motorcycle. Belang broke up the fight at that moment,” he said while reading his witness statement during his defence against the charge of murdering Nhaveen.
Ragesuthen said he, Gokulan, and another accused helped carry the injured accused back home to get treatment.
He said he then saw Belang take Nhaveen away on his motorcycle while Previin left on his own motorcycle, and he did not know what happened to them after that.
The man also admitted to mocking Nhaveen earlier along with another accused at a burger stall, though he could not recall the contents, and claimed that Nhaveen came with Previin to Jalan Kaki Bukit to ask why they had mocked Nhaveen, leading to the scuffle between them.
Answering questions from Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohd Amril Johari, Ragesuthen also denied that he, Gokulan, and the two other accused subsequently went to Padang Openg and continued the attack on Nhaveen.
Asked whether throughout the previous trial he had ever raised the fact that the accused’s friend passed out after being hit by Previin, Ragesuthan admitted that the matter had never been told in court.
Mohd Amril: No such testimony was presented at the prosecution stage that the accused’s friend was injured after being hit by Previin. Ragesuthan: I told the police. Mohd Amril: No, during the prosecution, we never even heard that the accused’s friend was injured and passed out, right? Ragesuthan: Right. Mohd Amril: So you agree this is the first time you are informing us that, first, the accused’s friend was hit by Previin and second, the accused’s friend passed out? Ragesuthan: Yes.
Ragesuthen also said he did not manhandle Previin, including trying to put him in a “neck lock,” but instead only held Previin while trying to break up the fight.
He also denied calling Nhaveen’s mother, T. Shanti, on the night of the incident to tell her that Nhaveen would not be returned until “the matter/issue is settled,” and denied mocking Nhaveen using insulting words including “potte” (effeminate/sissy).
Meanwhile, Gokulan said in his witness statement that he saw Previin hit another accused on the face with a helmet until he passed out on Jalan Kaki Bukit before hearing a loud scream and going to see what was happening.
He also disagreed with the prosecution’s suggestion that he and the three other accused beat Previin on the night of the incident or continued the attack on Nhaveen at Padang Openg.
During today’s proceedings, another accused also gave a nearly identical witness statement. The prosecution was handled by Mohd Amril, Yazid Mustaqim, and Noor Azura Zulkiflee, while the four accused were represented by lawyers Maanveer Singh Dhillon, R. Thevan, and Lim Sheng Zhe.
Previously, the Court of Appeal ordered Ragesuthen, Gokulan, and two other individuals who were minors at the time of the incident to enter their defene on the charge of murdering Nhaveen after allowing the prosecution’s appeal against the High Court’s decision to acquit and discharge them on October 3, 2023.
The four accused were also ordered to enter their defence on the charge of injuring Nhaveen’s friend, Previin, near the Karpal Singh Learning Centre on Jalan Kaki Bukit, Gelugor, between 11pm and 12 midnight on June 9, 2017.
Nhaveen passed away on June 15, 2017, after six days of treatment at the Penang Hospital due to severe injuries he suffered in the incident.
The trial before Judge Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid continues today. — Bernama

Title: Win-win for Petronas, Petros must pass commercial test
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — A Petronas-Petros settlement cannot credibly be described as “win-win” if the commercial consequences for one side are treated as irrelevant, one analyst says.
Samirul Ariff Othman from Global Asia Consulting was responding to Sarawak senator Datuk Ahmad Ibrahim’s statement that commercial considerations involving Petronas cannot override Sarawak’s constitutional rights. Ahmad was rebutting former law minister Datuk Zaid Ibrahim, who warned that Petronas could lose billions in business if Petros assumes a larger role in Sarawak’s gas sector.
Samirul said the latest argument also had to be read against the framework agreed by the federal and Sarawak governments in May last year.
Under the May 21, 2025 Joint Declaration signed by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg, Petros was recognised as Sarawak’s gas aggregator, but it also recognises Petronas’ continued aggregator role and affirms Petronas’s continuing responsibilities under the 1974 Petroleum Development Act. The declaration further provided that Petronas’s existing arrangements with third parties for LNG would remain unaffected.
Abang Johari subsequently described the arrangement as a “win-win” for Petros and Petronas, saying it preserved Petronas’s existing role while recognising Petros as gas aggregator.
Samirul said this made it difficult to argue now that Petronas’s commercial position was irrelevant to the eventual arrangement.
“The May declaration was not simply an acknowledgement of Petros’s role. It was a balance. Petros was recognised as one of the aggregators, but Petronas’s existing business and responsibilities were also expressly preserved.”
“Saying commercial considerations cannot override rights is not the same as saying commercial considerations do not matter. But it is still moving away from the logic of the very agreement that was described as win-win.”
“This was agreed upon by both the federal and Sarawak governments. You cannot ignore the parts intended to protect Petronas’s existing commercial position.”
Court has not settled rights
Samirul said Ahmad’s argument assumed a legal position that had yet to be settled.
“If Sarawak has a legal right, then of course that right does not disappear simply because another party will bear commercial costs.”
“But what exactly are Sarawak’s rights now? That is precisely the issue still before the courts. You cannot say Sarawak is entitled to a particular outcome because of the law when the scope of that entitlement has not yet been decided.”
The Federal Court is set to hear the case in January 2027, with Samirul adding that all parties  should allow that process to run its course.
“The proper thing is to let the court decide what the law actually requires. Until then, both sides are advancing legal claims. Neither side can treat its own interpretation as though it is already the settled legal position.”
What could a ‘win-win’ model look like?
In the spirit of the May 2025 framework, Samirul said one possible commercial model would be for Sarawak to take a larger role not only in the returns from the petroleum industry, but also in the investment and risks involved in creating that value.
Samirul said this could take the form of greater equity participation, co-investment, joint ventures and infrastructure ownership.
“Greater control should normally be accompanied by greater responsibility. Greater return should normally be accompanied by greater exposure to risk. This is what it means to do business.”
He said this would allow both sides to share the gains when projects succeed as well as the risks when they do not. Petronas and Petros had already shown that such cooperation was possible, including through potential gas development in the Lundu-Balingian area.
“The broader principle is that participation, investment, risk and reward can be shared rather than treated as mutually exclusive.”
“This converts the relationship from dividing rents into jointly creating value.”
Samirul said this was particularly important because Petronas still carries wider responsibilities, including upstream investment, maintaining production, LNG commitments and national energy security.
“If Petronas remains responsible for those functions, it must retain sufficient commercial authority and economic return to perform them. Petronas can perform several of these roles simultaneously. But it cannot do so without limits.”
Samirul said the challenge was therefore to enable Sarawak’s larger role without undermining Petronas’s ability to continue carrying its wider responsibilities. The ongoing dispute should also not be treated as a choice between a stronger Sarawak petroleum industry and a strong Petronas.
“A settlement that weakens either side would be a poor bargain. The real question is whether the eventual arrangement keeps control, capital, risk and returns aligned. Once those four become separated, the business model starts to weaken.”

Title: Retired JKR man killed as Proton Wira veers into opposite lane, collides head‑on with Persona in Setiu
Article:
BANDAR PERMAISURI, Oct 9 — An elderly man was killed after the Proton Wira he was driving collided with a Proton Persona at Kilometre 44 of Jalan Kuala Terengganu-Kota Bharu near Sungai Tong yesterday.
The victim, identified as Zulkefli Daud, 72, a retired Public Works Department (JKR) employee from Kampung Jeli Seberang, Jeli, Kelantan, died while being taken to hospital.
Setiu police chief Supt Zahril Asri Mohd Zain said the accident occurred at about 5.30pm and was believed to have happened when the victim’s car suddenly veered into the opposite lane.
“The driver of the Proton Persona, a 41-year-old woman travelling from Kuala Terengganu towards Kota Bharu, was unable to avoid the car, resulting in a collision.
“The woman sustained minor injuries, while the victim died on the way to hospital. His body was later sent to the Setiu Hospital Forensic Unit for a post-mortem,” he said in a statement today.
Zahril Asri said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He also urged anyone who witnessed the accident to contact the Traffic Division of the Setiu District Police Headquarters to assist in the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Food Act overhaul: Online sales, pesticide residues and unsafe packaging now under tighter watch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Dewan Rakyat yesterday passed the Food (Amendment) Bill 2026 to strengthen food safety and quality controls and provide more comprehensive protection for consumers nationwide.
The amendments to the Food Act 1983 (Act 281), the first comprehensive review of the act, include higher penalties, controls on samples of food contact materials (FCMs), monitoring of online food sales and monitoring of pesticide residue levels in agricultural produce.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the higher penalties were not intended to burden food operators or small traders, but to serve as a deterrent and safeguard public health.
“The existing penalties are no longer commensurate with the offences committed, particularly in cases of food poisoning resulting in deaths, such as the food poisoning incident at Sekolah Menengah Sains Teluk Intan, which affected 60 students but resulted in a fine of only RM3,000, and the laksa kebok case in Kedah, which claimed two lives but resulted in a fine of only RM1,500 in 2018.
“No monetary value can be placed on human life. The higher penalties take into account the seriousness of the offences and are proportionate to the violations committed to ensure greater accountability among traders,” he said when winding up debate on the bill.
The bill, among others, provides for higher fines and longer maximum jail terms, including a fine of up to RM25,000 or imprisonment for up to five years, or both, for offences under regulations made pursuant to Act 281.
Dzulkefly said the Health Ministry (MOH) would also adopt a risk-based approach to enforcement, whereby minor technical offences would first be addressed through advice and health education, while serious offences under Section 11 or repeated offences by persistent offenders would be taken directly to court without a compound being issued.
On online food sales, he said 23,553 requests to block social media accounts and e-commerce platforms had been submitted between 2023 and September 2026 due to an increasingly worrying trend of non-compliance.
He said the amendments would strengthen the powers of the Director-General of Health to close premises or disclose information on dangerous products without having to wait for a court order, particularly in cases involving the use of false addresses.
Dzulkefly also expressed concern over the rising rate of non-compliance with the maximum residue limit (MRL) for pesticides in vegetables sold on the local market, which increased from nine per cent in 2023 to 14.1 per cent between January and June 2026.
He also gave an assurance that the Health Ministry would provide a grace period and implement educational enforcement in phases during the transition to enforcement of the amended act to avoid adversely affecting the industry and small traders.
To ensure integrity among authorised officers, Dzulkefly said body cameras had been in use since 2022, alongside the digital use of the Malaysia Food Safety Information System (FoSIM), to reduce room for discretion and curb corruption.
The sitting was adjourned until 3.30pm today for the tabling of Budget 2027. — Bernama

Title: Tawau police arrest 14 boys after playground fight with weapons goes viral on social media
Article:
TAWAU, Oct 9 — Police arrested 14 male students yesterday in connection with a group student fight involving weapons at the Taman Ambar Playground, Jalan Kuhara here last Monday.
Tawau District Police Chief ACP Rosdi Mat Jusoh said the Criminal Investigation Division of the Tawau District Police Headquarters detained the suspects, aged between 12 and 14, to assist with the investigation.
“Police received a report regarding the fight at 6pm last Monday. Preliminary investigations found that the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding between two students before a fight broke out, which subsequently involved several other students.
“A viral video recording of the incident also helped police identify the individuals and their respective roles. In addition, police seized a mobile phone and a black bicycle believed to be related to the investigation,” he said in a statement here today.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 148 of the Penal Code and Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
“Investigations are underway to determine the involvement and role of each arrested individual. Furthermore, the police are obtaining original video recordings, as well as recording statements from witnesses and the detainees.
“At the same time, the police are also awaiting the victim’s medical report and cooperating with the school authorities and the Tawau District Education Office regarding the case,” he added.
Rosdi urged members of the public who witnessed the incident or possess any related information to come forward and assist with the investigation by contacting the investigating officer, Insp Robiatul Adawiyah Japri, at 016-918 9402 or by visiting the nearest police station.
In the meantime, he reminded the public that any act of rioting, attacking others, or using any object as a weapon is a serious offence that will not be compromised.
“Parents and guardians are advised to monitor their children’s associations and behaviour, while students are reminded not to get involved in fights, provoke others, or join groups that could lead to criminal behaviour,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Struggling with PTPTN? MoHE says come talk — restructure, defer, and keep repayments on track
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Borrowers facing difficulties settling their National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loan arrears are welcomed to come forward to negotiate for loan restructuring or apply for deferment according to permitted flexibilities.
The Ministry of Higher Education (MoHE), via a written reply published on the Parliament website yesterday, stated that the government is always mindful of the constraints faced by borrowers who are genuinely burdened in settling their loans.
“The total loan repayment arrears for the agency reached RM10.7 billion involving 1.16 million borrowers as of August 31, 2026,” according to the ministry.
The statement was issued in response to a question by Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson) regarding the latest total amount of PTPTN debt and the number of borrowers with arrears.
Various initiatives have been and will continue to be implemented to ensure the long-term fund sustainability of PTPTN’s business model, among which include strengthening loan management by improving loan terms and conditions to be more targeted towards those in need based on the agency’s capability.
“In addition, the effectiveness and efficiency of loan repayment collection will be enhanced through the implementation of enforcement and strategic cooperation with government and corporate agencies,” the ministry added. — Bernama

Title: ‘Clean air not a luxury’: Manufacturers in Malaysia demand Asean accelerate haze-free roadmap
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM) has pressed for decisive, measurable regional action from Asean to eliminate transboundary haze, warning that recurring pollution inflicts severe damage on public health, worker safety, and economic productivity.
The industrial group issued the appeal as severe haze blanketed the country, with Department of Environment (DOE) data recording 38 out of 68 national monitoring stations in the unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) bracket this morning, led by Seremban at 186.
